changes.before: Some saved information could not be read in this practice. Readable notes are shown; the original saved copy stays unchanged until you save or delete it.
changes.after: Some saved information could not be read in this practice. The system shows only the notes it could read; your original saved copy will not change unless you choose to save or delete it. This allows you to review and preserve anything that remains accurate, without risking loss of your previous information if new errors occur.
changes.reason: Refined for program-audience specificity. Clarified that only readable notes are shown, and explained why the saved copy is preserved until action is taken. Made the consequence of staff action explicit to help DHS/DSD staff understand practical data management. Avoided condescension and improved the connection between system behavior and staff choices.

findings.finding: The revised field0 text adds a substantive new explanation not present in the source. The source states: 'Some saved information could not be read in this practice. Readable notes are shown; the original saved copy stays unchanged until you save or delete it.' The rewrite adds: 'This allows you to review and preserve anything that remains accurate, without risking loss of your previous information if new errors occur.' This claim about the reason and benefit ('without risking loss...') is not stated or implied by the source, nor is there a source-based explanation that such review/preservation is a system-intended feature beyond the technical fact that data isn't overwritten until the user acts. The new explanation overstates intent and verges into systems interpretation rather than evidence from the code or existing field.
